goal:
CONTEXT: Today is 2026-08-05. The end user is a rapper recording vocals over MP3 instrumentals in Audacity. He wants to understand, in maximum depth, the vocal mixing + recording workflows/frameworks of VERIFIED, reputable people behind mainstream records of the last ~5 years (2021-2026). Genre weighting for the whole project is ~70% hip-hop/pop, 30% rock/other. He cares about repeatable FORMULAS/WORKFLOWS/FRAMEWORKS that are documented in depth and demonstrably worked on hit records — not one-off tricks or vibes.

EVIDENCE RULES (strict):
- Every claim about a person's process MUST carry a source URL. No unsourced assertions.
- Tier sources: A = primary long-form technical interviews/breakdowns (Sound on Sound 'Inside Track', Mix with the Masters, Pensado's Place, Produce Like A Pro, official mag interviews, the person's own videos/courses/masterclasses). B = reputable secondary (credible YouTube breakdowns, podcast clips, Reddit AMAs BY the person). C = forum hearsay — label it explicitly as unverified if you use it at all.
- Prefer direct quotes with exact source URLs. Quote accurately; do not paraphrase-quote.
- VERIFICATION: open each case study with proof of legitimacy: named hit records they mixed/recorded/produced, chart/award evidence, who they've worked with. 1 short block, sourced.
- RECENCY: the person must be tied to records that were mainstream within the last ~5 years. Older foundational interviews are fine as EVIDENCE if the person is still relevant.
- If a roster name turns out to have thin/no real documentation, say so in one line, drop them, and substitute the best-documented peer you find. Depth over roster completion.

OUTPUT FILES: Write ONE markdown file per person using the write tool, at the exact folder path given in your mission. Filename: firstname-lastname.md (lowercase, hyphenated). Use EXACTLY this template:

# <Name>
- **Role:** <mix engineer / recording engineer / producer / vocal producer / artist>
- **Verified credits:** <hit records + chart/award proof, with source URLs>
- **Recent mainstream relevance:** <2021-2026 records>
- **Evidence base:** <count by tier + list of all source URLs used>

## Vocal Philosophy
<their stated approach to vocals, with sourced quotes>

## The Vocal Chain (as documented)
<ordered signal chain: hardware/plugins in order, actual settings where documented (ratio/attack/release/threshold/EQ freqs/etc), DAW, what's fixed vs song-specific. If they have a repeatable template/framework, spell it out step by step. This is the core of the file — go DEEP.>

## Recording / Tracking Side
<mic choices, mic chains, gain staging, room treatment, comping/stacking, tuning workflow — whatever is documented>

## Signature Moves
<2-5 techniques they are known for, each sourced>

## Direct Quotes
<bulleted verbatim quotes, each with source URL>

## What To Steal
<5-10 concrete, tool-agnostic takeaways a beginner could apply (name free/stock plugin equivalents where a paid plugin is mentioned)>

RETURN FORMAT (your final message, compact): one block per person:
### <Name> — <role>
Credits: <one line> | Relevance: <one line>
Chain: <ordered one-line signal chain>
Signature moves: <comma list>
Top quote: "..." (<URL>)
Evidence: A:<n> B:<n> C:<n>
End with: FILES WRITTEN: <list of absolute paths>, plus any roster swaps you made and why.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- ALWAYS pass workflow: "none" on every web_search call. Use fetch_content to pull full text of the strongest sources (Sound on Sound, MWTM transcripts, interviews) rather than relying on search snippets.
- You may ONLY write files inside your assigned lane folder. Do not create or edit any other files.
- Do not launch subagents yourself.
- STOP RULES: stop researching a person once you have their chain + settings + 3+ sourced quotes, or once two consecutive searches add nothing new. Aim for depth per person, not endless breadth.
- Minimum research bar: at least 10 distinct web_search queries across your lane and at least 5 full fetch_content reads of primary sources.

YOUR MISSION:
LANE: New-wave / rage / underground hip-hop vocal sound — the lane closest to the user's taste (he named wifiskeleton, Lucki, Kanye, Playboi Carti, Lil Uzi Vert).
TARGETS (verify who actually engineers/mixes each artist; swap freely toward whoever is documented): Kesha Lee (Lil Uzi Vert's longtime recording engineer — documented interviews exist), whoever engineered/mixed Playboi Carti's MUSIC (2025) and Whole Lotta Red — find the actual credited mix/recording engineers and any interviews, Yeat's engineer(s) and the documented rage-vocal chain, F1lthy / Working on Dying (Lucki's production + recording world), wifiskeleton (likely self-mixed — find ANY documented process: interviews, Discord/streams, breakdowns; label thin evidence honestly), Ken Carson / Destroy Lonely / Opium engineers, Drain Gang (whitearmor, Bladee, Ecco2k — famously self-produced/self-mixed, documented techniques), Yung Lean / Gud / Whitearmor adjacent if useful.
SOURCE SEAM: artist/engineer interviews (The FADER, Complex, Pitchfork, Our Generation Music, Kaine's 'The Come Up' style YouTube interviews), Twitch/YouTube stream breakdowns, Reddit AMAs by the actual engineers, MasterClass/course content if it exists, plugin demos they appeared in.
KEY DECISIONS FOR YOU: (1) the rage/pluggnb vocal formula — distortion/saturation choices, Auto-Tune settings as an instrument, how vocals sit ON TOP of blown-out beats, (2) self-mixed artists' actual DAW + chain where documented (this matters to the user — he self-mixes), (3) ad-lib/vocal-layering architecture (Carti/Uzi style), (4) what's deliberately 'lo-fi/wrong' vs polished, and why it works. Honesty requirement: this scene is under-documented vs mainstream — clearly separate DOCUMENTED fact from community reconstruction, and say when something is fan-reverse-engineered.

# Research: New-Wave / Rage / Underground Hip-Hop Vocal Sound — Verified Engineers & Workflows (2021-2026)

## Summary
This lane's documentation is uneven: one engineer (Kesha Lee) has full Tier-A chain documentation via Sound on Sound; the rage-vocal core (Yeat, Carti, Opium) is verified at the level of *who does what* and *how sessions run*, but plugin-level chains are almost nowhere published by the actual people — most "rage vocal chain" content is fan/commercial reverse-engineering and is labeled C-tier throughout. The most valuable verified, stealable formulas are: Kesha Lee's complete Uzi chain (Auto-Tune-first, vocals-louder-than-beat), Yeat's documented self-engineering + 90-track ad-lib stack architecture, F1lthy's documented bus-and-clip beat framework that defines how vocals must sit, and the consistent team pipeline (Lidsky records/mixes → Roark Bailey mixes flagships → Colin Leonard masters) behind Opium.

## Findings
1. **Kesha Lee is the lane's deepest documented engineer.** Sound on Sound's *Inside Track* (Dec 2017) publishes her complete *Luv Is Rage 2* / "How To Talk" chain: per-track Antares Auto-Tune (retune 20 → 12-5, first insert, monitored live in the cans) → Waves De-Esser → Avid EQ3 7-band → Waves C1 gate; delay aux (Mod Delay II half-note, 43% feedback → R-Verb Hall 1 with highs cut → S1 imager); vocal bus (De-Esser @4.23kHz → EQ3 HPF 96.4Hz, cuts @200/500, +6.52kHz → RComp → SSL E-Channel → CLA-3A → RN Digital Detailer → MCL-2269); beat ducked 1-2dB under vocals; no master-bus plugins, -7 to -9dB headroom. She remains Uzi's recording engineer through *Pink Tape* (2023). [Sound on Sound](https://www.soundonsound.com/techniques/inside-track-lil-uzi-vert) [MusicBrainz](https://musicbrainz.org/release/484375b0-1b63-4469-9c57-f60d08462226)
2. **Playboi Carti's *MUSIC* (2025, #1 Billboard 200, 298k units) is mixed by Marcus Fritz (Fritz Owens)**, who also recorded most tracks; Johnathan Turner, Mike Dean, Rafael Fai Bautista mixed singles; O...
